common_name: Domino Coreopsis (Bicolor Red-Brown Center with Yellow Tips)

planting.note: Direct sow in spring in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Domino bears bicolor flowers with a deep red-brown center zone and bright yellow petal tips, a bold ring pattern typical of plains coreopsis selections.

directions: Direct sow in well-drained, lean, average soil in full sun; plains coreopsis tolerates poor, dry soils better than richer garden beds. Domino bears small, single flowers with a bold, contrasting pattern, a deep red-brown center ring surrounded by bright yellow tips, on a compact, airy plant that self-sows readily to naturalize a sunny meadow or wildflower planting. Its fine, uniform pattern makes it a strong choice for mass plantings and pollinator gardens. Deadhead to prolong bloom or allow seed heads to mature and drop for reseeding the following year.

common_name: Mercury Rising Coreopsis (Deep Red-Maroon Large-Flowered Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Mercury Rising bears deep, saturated red-maroon flowers, part of the Big Bang series of large-flowered coreopsis hybrids.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun. Mercury Rising bears large, single flowers in a deep, saturated red-maroon rarely seen in coreopsis, part of the Big Bang breeding series developed for large flower size and extended bloom, standing out dramatically among the more common yellow and bicolor tickseed cultivars. It blooms heavily from early summer into fall and draws bees and small pollinators, tolerating heat and humidity well once established. Shear the plant back by about a third after the first flush of bloom to encourage continued flowering, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring if the center begins to thin.
